Both actually. You may go on your .onion forum to complain about the communist party, but you won't say so in real life because they will kill you.

Finding ways around it don't always make the cut. For example, of course people in China can get around the firewall, but what about non internet users? What about non techies? The masses of people still have their experiences censored, and can easily be manipulated by state propaganda on more mainstream platforms like billboards or radio or television. Until a critical mass of people are not only aware of, but bothered by the censorship, the censorship will still be effective.

People will always find ways around it, but that doesn't mean it isn't working. As long as the information doesn't become widely known, the censorship has succeeded, if a few people manage to find out, they can be handled.
